# The door to Kirock's detective attraction

2026-11-04, Asia/Seoul. The user explicitly asks for Sherlock-Holmes-theme-park detail in every button and interaction. The previous flat teal composition reads as a web page with a mascot, not a place to enter. Preserve readable evidence and the actual photograph while making the surrounding world tactile.

## Plan before implementation

Palette: midnight street `#101d25`, painted door `#1e393d`, antique brass `#cda563`, amber light `#f5ce81`, ticket ivory `#f5e9ce`, seal burgundy `#803e39`. Cormorant display type supplies an engraved storybook voice; system sans remains for evidence and controls. No lettering is baked into button bitmaps: all ten languages remain accessible live text.

Composition: a wide, softly lit miniature Baker Street entrance surrounds a clearly separated central game surface. The detective and title introduce the attraction; an actual photograph hangs in a case frame. Sample entry is a raised brass doorplate with a bell; uploading uses a perforated evidence ticket with a camera. Smaller buttons have consistent hardware, not random embellishments.

```
     gaslight       agency crest / utility dials        gaslight
          engraved title       detective        hanging case file
          invitation + premise                  actual photograph
          brass bell / sample                   numbered suspect tabs
          photo evidence ticket                 comic response
                    three investigation stages

     inside the case: scene photograph | clipped investigation notebook
                 witness slips → pinned comparison → hypothesis cards
```

The opening uses the same street and door vocabulary. Interactions should feel physical: press depression, a short bell swing on hover/focus, a selected brass tab, a heard mark and an objection seal. The motion-reduction preference disables decorative movement. Utility controls remain named and at least 44px high. Faces, colors and effects never depend on guilt before a verdict.

## Critique and scope

An ornate wallpaper behind every sentence would repeat the rejected Victorian clutter. Concentrate the illustrative environment at entry, place body text on predictable dark or paper surfaces, and use hardware to communicate actions and state. Every button family receives an intentional treatment, including settings, preview, testimony, confrontation, deduction, photo editing, verdict and sharing. A single generated scene plus two blank material assets creates a coherent family; decorative SVG props stay crisp and labels remain editable.

The mystery engine, shared snapshots, expiry/deletion and runtime AI contract do not change. Kiro development usage is distinct from player authentication and from the optional vision API. New art and overall integration are Codex work; any new Kiro source is attributed only after its real run and output are observed.

description: Learn how to create full-stack web applications with the Next.js App Router.

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

This **Getting Started** section will help you create your first Next.js app and learn the core features you'll use in every project.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

## Next Steps

---
title: Next.js Glossary
nav_title: Glossary
description: A glossary of common terms used in Next.js.
---

This glossary defines common terms used throughout the Next.js documentation, including terms related to routing, rendering, and caching.

# A

## App Router

The Next.js router introduced in version 13, built on top of React Server Components. It uses file-system based routing and supports layouts, nested routing, loading states, error handling, and more. Learn more in the [App Router documentation](/docs/app).

## App Shell

A per-route prerender containing the parts of a page that don't depend on URL data. Cached content is included when its [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes, since the shell is reused for longer than shorter-lived content stays fresh. Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce one that also includes session data, cached per session on the client. Used as the default prefetch payload during client navigations, the loading state when a [per-link prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) is not ready, and the fallback for [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components).

# B

## Build time

The stage when your application is being compiled. During build time, Next.js transforms your code into optimized files for production, generates static pages, and prepares assets for deployment. See the [`next build` CLI reference](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-build-options).

# C

## Cache Components

A feature that enables component and function-level caching using the [`"use cache"` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). Cache Components allows you to mix static, cached, and dynamic content within a single route by prerendering a static HTML shell that's served immediately, while dynamic content streams in when ready. Configure cache duration with [`cacheLife()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife), tag cached data with [`cacheTag()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag), and invalidate on-demand with [`updateTag()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag). Learn more in the [Cache Components guide](/docs/app/getting-started/caching).

## Catch-all Segments

Dynamic route segments that can match multiple URL parts using the `[...folder]/page.js` syntax. These segments capture all remaining URL segments and are useful for implementing features like documentation sites or file browsers. Learn more in [Dynamic Route Segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments).

## Client Bundles

JavaScript bundles sent to the browser. Next.js splits these automatically based on the [module graph](#module-graph) to reduce initial payload size and load only the necessary code for each page.

## Client Component

A React component that runs in the browser. In Next.js, Client Components can also be rendered on the server during initial page generation. They can use state, effects, event handlers, and browser APIs, and are marked with the [`"use client"` directive](#use-client-directive) at the top of a file. Learn more in [Server and Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).

## Client-side navigation

A navigation technique where the page content updates dynamically without a full page reload. Next.js uses client-side navigation with the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link), keeping shared layouts interactive and preserving browser state. Learn more in [Linking and Navigating](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#client-side-transitions).

## Client Cache

An in-memory cache in the browser that stores [RSC Payload](#rsc-payload) for visited and prefetched routes. During [client-side navigation](#client-side-navigation), Next.js serves cached [layouts](#layout) and [loading states](#loading-ui) instantly without a server request. Pages are not cached by default but are reused during browser back/forward navigation.

The client cache is cleared on page refresh. It can be invalidated programmatically with [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag), [`router.refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), [`cookies.set`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), or [`cookies.delete`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies).

You can configure the client cache duration with [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes) globally, or per-route via the `stale` property in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#client-cache-behavior) (recommended).

## Code Splitting

The process of dividing your application into smaller JavaScript chunks based on routes. Instead of loading all code upfront, only the code needed for the current route is loaded, reducing initial load time. Next.js automatically performs code splitting based on routes. Learn more in the [Package Bundling guide](/docs/app/guides/package-bundling).

# Detective Hypothesis Board — Requirements

**Feature:** Manual six-world hypothesis scratchpad for Room of Suspects.  
**Author:** Kiro (2026-10-31). Inherited application code is Codex work; this feature is new Kiro work.

---

## Overview

Players reason by elimination. After examining cross-examination dialogue, they need a place to track
which of the six possible (culpritId × fact) worlds they have ruled out through their own deduction.
The board is a personal scratchpad — it never knows the answer, never evaluates the player's logic,
and never submits a verdict.

---

## Requirements

### REQ-1 Pure hypothesis builder (TypeScript, no UI)

- **REQ-1.1** `buildHypotheses(suspects, displayOrder)` accepts a `readonly Suspect[]` and a
  `readonly SuspectId[]` display order, and returns exactly six `Hypothesis` objects in a
  deterministic order: for each suspect in display order, `fact=false` then `fact=true`.
- **REQ-1.2** Each `Hypothesis` carries a stable `id` string derived solely from `culpritId` and
  `fact` (no randomness, no runtime state). The format is `<culpritId>-<fact>` (e.g. `"s0-false"`).
- **REQ-1.3** The builder must not mutate the input arrays or objects.
- **REQ-1.4** The builder has no dependency on DOM, React, Next.js, AI, storage, solver, or private
  answer data. It imports only from `./types`.
- **REQ-1.5** The module exports `buildHypotheses`, the `Hypothesis` type, and the `HypothesisId`
  type directly from `src/lib/game/hypothesis.ts`.

### REQ-2 HypothesisBoard component

- **REQ-2.1** Default export `HypothesisBoard` is a `'use client'` React component with exact props:
  ```ts
  { suspects: readonly Suspect[]; locale: Locale; factLabels: readonly [string, string] }
  ```
  `factLabels[0]` describes the `false` event; `factLabels[1]` describes the `true` event.
- **REQ-2.2** The component owns all eliminated-world state locally via `useState`. The parent never
  passes a case, solution, testimony, or solver instance.
- **REQ-2.3** Each of the six hypothesis cards is a `<button>` that toggles the card between
  `possible` and `eliminated`. When eliminated, `aria-pressed="true"` is set on the button.
- **REQ-2.4** Each card displays: the suspect's `displayName`, the matching fact label, and explicit
  visible text for the current state (`가능` / `제외됨` in Korean, `Possible` / `Eliminated` in
  English). Color alone must not be the only state indicator.
- **REQ-2.5** The component never reads from or writes to a backend, localStorage, or cookies.

### REQ-3 Counter, reset, and edge-case labels

- **REQ-3.1** A localized reset button (data-testid `hypothesis-reset`) restores all six cards to
  `possible`. Its label is `가설 초기화` (Korean) / `Reset hypotheses` (English).
- **REQ-3.2** The component displays a remaining-count line, e.g. `남은 가설: 4 / 6` / `Remaining: 4 / 6`.
- **REQ-3.3** When exactly one card remains possible, that card gets an additional label
  `내가 남긴 가설` (Korean) / `My remaining theory` (English). The board must never assert that
  a player-selected theory is verified correct or that it identifies the culprit. Specifically,
  the last-card label must not claim `정답` (correct answer), imply `정답이에요`, or use any
  phrasing that presents the remaining theory as a confirmed truth rather than the player's own
  working hypothesis.
- **REQ-3.4** When zero cards remain possible, the component shows an explanatory message inviting
  the player to restore cards using the reset button. It must not say "you are wrong" or anything
  equivalent.

### REQ-4 CSS hooks and test IDs

- **REQ-4.1** Outer wrapper element has `className="hypothesis-board"` and
  `data-testid="hypothesis-board"`.
- **REQ-4.2** The grid container has `className="hypothesis-grid"`.
- **REQ-4.3** Each card `<button>` has `className="hypothesis-card"` and
  `data-testid="hypothesis-card-<stableId>"` (e.g. `hypothesis-card-s0-false`).
- **REQ-4.4** The reset button has `data-testid="hypothesis-reset"`.
- **REQ-4.5** No inline styles that would override Codex CSS. No new CSS files introduced.

### REQ-5 Localization

- **REQ-5.1** All UI labels exist in Korean (`ko`) and English (`en`).
- **REQ-5.2** The component selects language via the `locale` prop. No other i18n mechanism is used.
- **REQ-5.3** `factLabels` come from the parent (derived from `publicSnapshot`) and are displayed
  verbatim; the component does not fabricate event descriptions.

### REQ-6 Game invariant compliance

- **REQ-6.1** The board never eliminates any hypothesis automatically.
- **REQ-6.2** The board never shows which hypothesis is correct.
- **REQ-6.3** The board is not a verdict submission mechanism.
- **REQ-6.4** The board adds no new evidence or factual claims beyond the labels supplied by the parent.

### REQ-7 Tests

- **REQ-7.1** `tests/hypothesis.test.ts` uses `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`.
- **REQ-7.2** Tests cover: all six suspect-ID permutations produce six hypotheses; ordering matches
  display order with false-before-true per suspect; all six IDs are unique per run; IDs are stable
  independent of display order; frozen input arrays and objects are not mutated.
- **REQ-7.3** No tests for invalid inputs (validation is upstream).
- **REQ-7.4** A source-level check may confirm `hypothesis.ts` does not import solver or private
  answer modules.

# Detective Hypothesis Board — Design **Feature:** Manual six-world hypothesis scratchpad. **Author:** Kiro (2026-10-31). --- ## Module: `src/lib/game/hypothesis.ts` ### Types ```ts export type HypothesisId = `${SuspectId}-false` | `${SuspectId}-true`; export type Hypothesis = { readonly id: HypothesisId; readonly culpritId: SuspectId; readonly fact: boolean; readonly suspectDisplayName: string; }; ``` `HypothesisId` is a branded template-literal type over the six legal combinations. Using a template literal keeps the type precise without a runtime enum. ### Builder ```ts export function buildHypotheses( suspects: readonly Suspect[], displayOrder: readonly SuspectId[], ): Hypothesis[] ``` Algorithm: 1. **Feature:** Reusable decorative SVG icon component for the Sherlock detective theme-park interface.  
**Author:** Kiro (2026-11-04). Inherited application code and app integration are Codex work;
this component is new Kiro work.  
**Workflow:** CLI-authored spec, not a native IDE spec workflow.

## Overview

The detective theme-park interface needs a small set of tactile, period-appropriate SVG icons that
can be scattered across buttons, headings, and decorative regions to communicate the physical world
of Baker Street. Each icon must be legible at 48 CSS pixels, express its referent through outline
only (no fills that obscure the parent element's surface), and carry no interactive semantics of its
own — parent buttons and labels already supply accessible names and roles.

---

## Requirements

### REQ-1 Component contract

- **REQ-1.1** The file exports a single default export named `DetectiveProp`.
- **REQ-1.2** Props:
  ```ts
  { kind: 'bell' | 'key' | 'camera' | 'seal' | 'pin' | 'footprints' | 'crest'; className?: string }
  ```
  No other props are accepted or forwarded to the SVG element.
- **REQ-1.3** The component requires no `'use client'` directive; it contains no state, effects,
  event handlers, or browser APIs, and may therefore be rendered as a Server Component.

### REQ-2 SVG output invariants

- **REQ-2.1** Every rendered SVG has `viewBox="0 0 48 48"`.
- **REQ-2.2** Every rendered SVG has `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`. These must
  never be absent or overridden.
- **REQ-2.3** No SVG element carries `role="img"`, a `<title>`, a `<desc>`, or any interactive
  role attribute. Accessible names are provided by parent controls.
- **REQ-2.4** All strokes use `currentColor`. Fills must be either `"none"` (transparent) or
  `currentColor` where a small solid region meaningfully reinforces silhouette readability;
  no hardcoded colour hex/rgb values.
- **REQ-2.5** No SVG `id` attributes, no `<defs>`, no `<use>`, no `<symbol>`, no
  `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, and no arbitrary HTML props spread onto SVG elements.
- **REQ-2.6** No external images, no `<image>` elements, no embedded font glyphs, no imported
  bitmap assets.

### REQ-3 CSS class

- **REQ-3.1** Every rendered SVG element has `className` set to `"detective-prop"` plus the
  caller-supplied `className` value (if provided), separated by a space. When `className` is
  absent the element carries exactly `"detective-prop"`.
- **REQ-3.2** The component introduces no new CSS file. Codex supplies styling for
  `.detective-prop` in the application stylesheet.

### REQ-4 Icon silhouettes

Each variant must be distinctly recognizable as its referent at 48 px, drawn from original
code-native SVG paths and shapes only.

- **REQ-4.1 `bell`** — a brass reception / concierge bell: a dome body, base plate, and a small
  button on top. No handle (a desk bell, not a hand bell). Stroke-only silhouette.
- **REQ-4.2 `key`** — an old skeleton key: circular bow (ring end) with a small circular cutout
  inside, a long narrow shaft, and two or three simple rectangular bits (teeth) extending from the
  blade end.
- **REQ-4.3 `camera`** — an antique folding / bellows camera: a trapezoidal or boxy outer body with
  a prominent circular lens in the centre and a simple rectangular viewfinder or handle detail.
  Stroke-only silhouette.
- **REQ-4.4 `seal`** — a scalloped wax seal circle: a circle with a scalloped or serrated outer
  edge and a simple check-mark (✓) drawn inside. No text baked into paths.
- **REQ-4.5 `pin`** — a map pushpin / thumbtack: a circular head at the top and a triangular or
  tapered spike pointing downward.
- **REQ-4.6 `footprints`** — two detective shoe-print silhouettes, one left and one right, arranged
  diagonally as if mid-stride. Each footprint is a simple filled oval-ish sole shape with a rounded
  toe end. No toes, no laces.
- **REQ-4.7 `crest`** — a detective crest combining two elements: a small deerstalker cap outline
  at the top and a magnifying glass outline below, arranged within the 48×48 canvas as a unified
  emblem. No pipe, no gun, no realistic eye.

### REQ-5 Prohibited content

- **REQ-5.1** No pipe, no gun, no realistic human eye.
- **REQ-5.2** No locale, game-state, guilt, solver, network, storage, animation, or event handling.
- **REQ-5.3** No import of any application module (engine, AI, server, locale, storage, Game, etc.).
- **REQ-5.4** No test that merely copies static SVG path strings back and asserts equality; tests
  are not part of the Kiro scope for this feature (spec only).

### REQ-6 Attribution and scope

- **REQ-6.1** `src/components/DetectiveProp.tsx` is Kiro work.
- **REQ-6.2** App integration (CSS, layout, import into scene components) is Codex work.
- **REQ-6.3** No existing file — including `Game.tsx`, `GameIcon.tsx`, and any page or layout — is
  modified by Kiro.

```
base:    rect x=6 y=34 w=36 h=4 rx=2
button:  circle cx=24 cy=14 r=2

```

- Inner cutout: smaller `<circle>` inside bow, radius ~4.

- Back peak: a short curved brim projecting right.
